svg.title: MARS as built: the model proposes, tested software computes
svg.desc: Five horizontal lanes. Callers (the mars console, the mars-bench benchmark, Python scripts and MCP clients) enter at the top. The console and the benchmark drive one bounded loop of at most 20 turns, which checks every proposed tool call against its schema, a stop request, an approval policy and a repeat-call cache before dispatching it, and records every call in a session record. MCP clients reach the tools through a server that applies a strict schema check. A dashed trust boundary separates the model side from the software side. Below it, a surface of 55 typed tools in five groups calls algorithms extracted from the Skynet pipeline and Afterglow, ported from Astromancer, or first-party, which read the data installed with the package, checksum-pinned optional bundles and remote astronomy services. Results return as structured results and artifacts.
svg.text: each turn: stop check → user notes → model call → fault log
decision and result, saved per call
a model’s request crosses only as a schema-valid call
Tool surface: 55 typed tools · 26 local · 22 remote · 7 mixed · stateless per call
